title: Haor farmers get early rice variety to beat flash floods
excerpt: BRRI dhan118 can be harvested 7 to 10 days earlier. Floods last year damaged crops worth about Tk 1,047 crore in the haor.
content:
Farmers in seven haor districts are getting an early-maturing rice variety, BRRI dhan118, to help them harvest before flash floods arrive, The Daily Star reported on Thursday (19 November). About 1,600 demonstration plots have been set up and 30 tonnes of seed distributed.

The variety can be harvested 7 to 10 days earlier than the varieties now grown. Flash floods between 26 April and 4 May last year damaged crops worth about Tk 1,047 crore on more than 49,000 hectares, the paper said.

Who is involved

The Daily Star quoted Md Rafiqul Islam, director general of the Bangladesh Rice Research Institute (BRRI), and Mohammad Zakir Hossain, senior information officer at the agriculture ministry.

Why it matters

In the haor, a few days can decide whether a family keeps its only rice crop of the year. Food security and climate adaptation NGOs in Sunamganj, Netrokona, Kishoreganj and nearby districts can link seed, early warning and harvest support.

What to watch

Yields from the demonstration plots in April and May, and whether seed supply is scaled up after this Boro season.
